correctness.rationale: For n>=2 and 0<=s<1, a and b obey a^2+(n+1)sa/sqrt(n)+s^2=1 and b^2-a^2=sqrt(n)sa, verified by direct substitution into their closed radicals. The farther-shifted squared distance of any transformed unit-ball point is at most 1-sqrt(n)sa(|u_1|-1/sqrt(n))^2. Equality gives precisely both stated contact latitudes for s>0. At each of 2n paired regular-simplex contacts the active constraint has normal parallel to the transformed contact. Weighted mean zero and covariance identity imply tr(A)<=n for every arbitrary translated/rotated competing ellipsoid y+A B_n with A positive definite; eigenvalue AM-GM gives det(A)<=1, equality only A=I and y=0. Thus optimality and uniqueness are global, not merely within ellipsoids of revolution. The separate beta-integral volume expression and semiaxis asymptotics prove the thin-lens limit. An embedded self-contained checker reproduces exact rational identities, support inequalities, contact-frame identities and asymptotic sample checks, none of which replace the analytic continuum proof.

originality.rationale: The concrete all-dimensional John ellipsoid, semiaxes, equality contacts, and thin-lens volume ratio are not stated or mathematically implied by the inspected closest writings. Finch calculates different lens measures; a published same-lens mean-width formula concerns an intrinsic functional, not ellipsoid optimization; Güler and Gürtuna study balls clipped by parallel planes, not intersections of two curved ball caps; and Ivanov et al. provide general ellipsoid-of-revolution theory without this lens specialization. Published-record and literature searches were checked by mathematical implication rather than title alone. Absolute historical priority remains unproved.

Semantic published-record search cannot establish global novelty or identify unpublished work.

value.rationale: Intersections of two equal balls form a canonical one-parameter family of ball-convex bodies, previously studied quantitatively via volume, mean width and support functions. The all-dimensional exact John ellipsoid is a natural geometric invariant not determined by those earlier formulas. The proof establishes global optimizer rigidity, an offset-independent contact-latitude law, and a strictly positive explicit thin-lens fraction. These exact structural facts can serve as a benchmark for ellipsoid approximation of lens-type bodies; no speculative general theorem is required for value. It is not a parameter substitution of the spherical-slab formula or mere numerical recomputation.
